reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it describes a creator-run thank-you giveaway offering one $100 Ulta gift card after reaching 1,000 subscribers. Participation involves subscribing and commenting, and an address is requested only after contacting the winner to send the prize. the available video evidence does not verify delivery, but it describes no payment requirement, credential request, deceptive destination, or supported connection to the separately listed affiliate links.

citations.quote: one lucky winner will win a. Hundred dollar gift card to Ulta
Do is just make sure that you are subscribed to my channel and then down. Below in the comment section name one thing that you would buy with this gift. Card
I will just directly. Message you here on YouTube to tell you that you won and get your address and everything like that. So I can send you
And also this giveaway will be open for one week only.
Giveaway Rules: 1) Subscribe to my channel 2) Leave a comment sharing one product you would buy with this $100 Ulta gift card!

opening.argument: The central offer is a $100 gift card tied directly to audience actions, not an unconditional gift. The viewer must subscribe and comment with a product they would buy, while only one person can receive the promised reward. The proposed follow-up also requires the selected person to provide an address through a direct message. That is a clear reward-for-engagement funnel: the creator obtains subscriptions, comments, and contact information in exchange for a low-barrier chance at a valuable gift card. The fact that the action is easy does not make the acquisition pathway trustworthy; it makes participation easier to scale.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the requirements “participation” does not remove the solicitation. The stated prize is expressly conditioned on subscribing and commenting, and the proposed delivery process includes collecting an address after direct contact. The defense establishes what viewers are asked to do, but it does not establish that the gift card was actually purchased, delivered, or independently verifiable.

citations.quote: all you need to. Do is just make sure that you are subscribed to my channel and then down. Below in the comment section name one thing that you would buy with this gift. Card
get your address and everything like that. So I can send you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted conditions show ordinary contest entry requirements, not fraud. Subscription and a comment are the announced entry mechanism, while an address is requested only from the person who wins so the stated prize can be sent. These quotes show a chance-based giveaway and a proposed delivery step; they do not show payment, credential theft, or a demand that viewers follow an external claim process.

citations.quote: one lucky winner will win a. Hundred dollar gift card to Ulta
I will just directly. Message you here on YouTube to tell you that you won and get your address and everything like that. So I can send you

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a substantial $100 gift-card promise, a single winner, a short closing window, and collection of an address through a direct message. The description fixes a deadline and says the winner will be messaged, while the video describes the reward as dependent on subscribing and commenting. That combination creates urgency and concentrates the next step in a private contact channel. The supplied material does not independently verify the prize, the random selection, or delivery, so the viewer is being asked to act on an attractive promise before those material facts are established.

citations.quote: Giveaway closes on 4/6 at 5:00pm EST
The winner will be messaged directly through Youtube by 4/7
And also this giveaway will be open for one week only.
one lucky winner will win a. Hundred dollar gift card to Ulta

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the deadline and direct message as neutral logistics, but those are precisely the mechanisms that create time pressure and move the winner interaction into a private channel. Its statement that no payment or credential request appears does not answer the more basic concern: viewers are urged to enter for a valuable reward whose existence and delivery are not established by the supplied evidence.

citations.quote: Giveaway closes on 4/6 at 5:00pm EST
The winner will be messaged directly through Youtube by 4/7

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A stated closing date and a private message to the selected winner are ordinary administration for a one-week giveaway, not evidence of deception. The offer identifies one winner and explains when the giveaway closes; nothing quoted requires money, account credentials, or an external verification payment. The absence of proof of later delivery is a limitation of the record, not proof that the promotion is fraudulent.

citations.quote: this giveaway will be open for one week only
The winner will be messaged directly through Youtube by 4/7

opening.argument: Although the speaker frames the video as a thank-you to subscribers, its operative function is promotional: the title foregrounds an Ulta gift-card giveaway, and the rules direct viewers to subscribe and comment. The creator links the reward to measurable channel engagement, using gratitude and an enthusiastic personal presentation to encourage participation. The description also places the giveaway alongside business and referral links, showing a broader promotional context. A friendly thank-you framing does not change that viewers are being steered toward an engagement action for a promised reward.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the apparent mechanics but does not confront the promotional function. The title explicitly advertises the giveaway, and the rules convert gratitude into subscriptions and comments. Saying the listed links are not proven to be part of the giveaway does not change the central steering mechanism: engagement is requested in return for a chance at the advertised reward.

citations.quote: ULTA GIFT CARD GIVEAWAY! [CLOSED]
Giveaway Rules: 1) Subscribe to my channel 2) Leave a comment sharing one product you would buy with this $100 Ulta gift card!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotional presentation is not itself a scam. The title and rules accurately describe a creator-run giveaway, and the requested actions are visible entry conditions rather than payment or a deceptive destination. The quoted social links show where to keep up with the creator, but they do not establish that viewers must use them to claim the prize or that the giveaway is fraudulent.
